title: 01 Notebook Basics
description: How long is a day? One small project that tours every core cell: JavaScript, Python, a chart, a slider and a live HTML card.

title: AI 1 Build With Prompts
description: No coding needed: describe what you want and a model writes the cell. Build a live aquarium in four prompts, then fix a broken cell with AI Fix and learn what makes a prompt work.

title: AI 2 Generate a Whole Notebook
description: One prompt, a whole notebook. How Generate notebook works, what a strong prompt includes, a prompt builder that writes one for you, and four prompts to try.

title: AI 3 A 3D Solar System
description: A three.js Solar System from three prompts: planets where they really are today, real spin and tilt, Saturn's rings, follow a planet, click for facts.

title: AI 4 A Game From Two Prompts
description: Gravity Courier, an original arcade game: deliver parcels between orbiting planets, with a tuning panel that changes the game mid-flight.

title: AI 5 A Living Ecosystem
description: Grass, rabbits and foxes in a live agent simulation, then Python finds the predator–prey cycle in the history. Three prompts.

title: AI 6 Research With Search
description: Has my city got warmer? Web search supplies current figures with sources and the right data to use, then 75 years of real daily temperatures answer the question, with warming stripes.

title: 02 Sharing Data Between Cells
description: A shopping basket passed through JavaScript, Python, a chart, controls, a live HTML receipt and Lua, plus a budget planner built from a prompt that reads `nb`.

title: 03 Python to JavaScript to HTML
description: Is my bus late? Python works out the delays and JavaScript draws a departure board, twice: once as a snapshot it returns, once as a live HTML cell that follows a slider.

title: 04 Matplotlib & Data Science
description: When should we have the picnic? NumPy works through a year of weather, matplotlib plots it, and an interactive Vega-Lite calendar shows the same days.

title: 05 Live API → Analysis → Visualization
description: A week of real earthquakes from the USGS: fetch it in JavaScript, tidy it with pandas, then see the Ring of Fire appear on a world map.

title: 06 Interactive HTML Mini-Apps
description: Three small apps that work together through `nb`: a palette picker, a pixel editor and a live animation of your drawing, which Python then turns into a sprite sheet.

title: 07 Building a Report (End-to-End)
description: How did the school fair do? A real report: findings written by code, charts, a live what-if with sliders, and an Export that keeps it all working in one file.

title: 08 C Cells
description: C close to the machine: the first program in the classic C book and its whole-number trap, bit flags, and a Rule 30 pattern computed in C and drawn by an HTML cell.

title: 10 UI Controls
description: Design a creature with every kind of control (text, colour, slider, dropdown, buttons and more) and watch it redraw live, then read the same values from Python.

title: 11 Lua Cells
description: Lua makes a dungeon, an HTML cell turns it into a game you can play, and JavaScript checks it can be finished. With a guide to reading Lua.

title: 12 Lua ↔ JavaScript
description: Lua plays 5,000 games of Snakes and Ladders; JavaScript charts them, Python works out the odds, and a live board shows where players land.
